ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory electronic screening against the Spanish Financial Intelligence Unit (SEPBLAC) obligations, Spanish official PEP database, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN List, and INTERPOL red-flag source; screening must occur before accepting any relationship and continuously for each officer, shareholder, UBO and signatory; the compliance file must be preserved for at least 10 years under Law 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) - www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The chosen corporate name must be in Spanish orthography and Latin script; foreign words are permitted only if transliterated into Spanish characters and if not misleading regarding the company form; the name must end with 'Sociedad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.'; the name must not be identical or phonetically equivalent to any existing Spanish company name; signs beyond standard Spanish characters are not accepted.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Palabras o siglas reservadas a entidades de crédito, seguros y valores
Términos contrarios al orden público penal o civil
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Central Commercial Registry rejects a requested denomination, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registro Mercantil Central within one month of notification. If reconsideration is denied, a hierarchy appeal (recurso de alzada) must be lodged before the Directorate General for Legal Certainty (DGFeJ) of the Ministry of Justice within one month; court litigation before the administrative courts is available only after exhaustion of the administrative appeal. The name certificate expires after 90 days without formal incorporation, and a new reservation must be obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office may be established at a virtual or corporate-service-provider address for correspondence and administrative purposes, but for an LNG receiving terminal cryogenic piping contractor under ISIC 4322/NAICS 237120, the company must maintain a demonstrable physical operational site or project office in Spain at time of licensing, contract execution, and for construction supervision. A virtual address alone is not acceptable as substantive commercial presence for AML, sectoral licensing, or tax residence purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High quantified risk: approximately 70% probability of unannounced physical inspection by SEPBLAC, the Tax Agency, or the industrial safety authority within the first 3 years of operations, and 95% probability of at least one on-site verification before obtaining or renewing relevant gas infrastructure installation licenses.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 19-24, 28, 62, 63, 73-77, 210-212, 214-216 and 279-283; Law 18/2022 amended Article 4 to permit a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada to have minimum capital of EUR 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The relevant Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial), coordinated through the Ministry of Justice; the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) issues the company-name clearance certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) executed before a Spanish notary, followed by an application for registration with the relevant Provincial Commercial Registry and issuance of the definitive Spanish tax identification number.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum share capital is EUR 1, fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. There is no mandatory escrow account if the deed records the founders' joint and several responsibility for the reality of the cash contributions; alternatively, a Spanish bank certificate may evidence deposit into an account opened in the company's name under formation. If capital is below EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the aggregate reserve and capital reach EUR 3,000, and the shareholders bear additional liquidation liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. Notarial, registry, publication and professional charges are separate regulated or market-based costs; Spain has no single fixed state incorporation filing fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the shares subscribed by the founding shareholder under the deed of incorporation are approved and recorded as fully subscribed and paid; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, if a board structure is selected, [names] are appointed directors with the powers stated in the articles; (4) [name] is appointed secretary, if applicable; (5) the director is authorised to obtain the definitive NIF, register tax activities, open operating bank accounts, execute employment and supplier arrangements, and apply for all industrial, environmental, fire-safety and occupational permits required for cryogenic piping activities.

governance_requirements.shareholder_meeting: The general meeting must approve annual accounts, profit allocation, director appointments and other reserved matters under the Companies Act and the articles.
governance_requirements.annual_accounts: Annual accounts must generally be approved within six months after financial year-end and filed with the Provincial Commercial Registry within one month after approval, subject to statutory exemptions and applicable filing rules.
governance_requirements.beneficial_ownership: Beneficial ownership information must be maintained and disclosed through the applicable notarial and commercial-registry systems, with additional declarations required for banking, AML and certain official procedures.
governance_requirements.foreign_shareholders: Non-resident shareholders may own 100% of the SL. Foreign individuals generally require a Spanish NIE and foreign companies require evidence of existence, authority and beneficial ownership, duly legalized or apostilled and translated into Spanish where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate structure and obtain foreign-investor identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish National Police Foreigners' Offices for NIE applications; Spanish notary and commercial registry system for corporate verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the SL management structure, shareholders, directors, registered office and financial year. Obtain NIEs for relevant non-resident individuals and Spanish NIFs for foreign corporate shareholders. Authenticate powers of attorney before a Spanish notary or through a legalized foreign instrument.
required_dossiers: NIE application and supporting corporate-purpose evidence
Foreign shareholder certificate of incorporation and current good-standing evidence
Board or shareholder authorization for investment
Apostille or consular legalization, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct identity inconsistencies, renew expired corporate certificates, replace defective powers of attorney and resubmit to the relevant Foreigners' Office or notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), Company Name Clearance Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names through the registry's electronic or postal procedure. Obtain the negative name certificate and reserve the approved name for the statutory validity period. Ensure the name is distinct from existing registered names and compatible with the legal form Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
Proposed company names in priority order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit alternative names if refused for similarity, prohibited wording or formal defects. Renew the certificate if it expires before deed execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare articles and capital subscription evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary selected for incorporation; Spanish bank if voluntary capital deposit is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association stating name, purpose, registered office, share capital, share classes, management form and rules for shareholder meetings. Subscribe and pay the capital. Either obtain a bank certificate or include the founders' statutory responsibility declaration in the deed.
required_dossiers: Evidence of capital deposit or founder responsibility declaration
Registered-office title, lease or use authorization
Description of the corporate purpose, including industrial contracting activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve notarial observations, amend articles, correct capital allocation or replace defective banking evidence before signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear personally or through valid power of attorney. Execute the escritura pública de constitución, including articles, shareholder contributions, management appointments, registered office and beneficial ownership information. Request an authorized electronic copy for tax and registry filings.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit certificate or responsibility declaration
Legalized foreign corporate documents and translations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Execute a corrective or supplementary notarial deed where the notary identifies omissions, inconsistencies or invalid powers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional NIF and register tax commencement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT), including the electronic census filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 with the incorporation deed or authorized electronic copy to obtain the provisional NIF. Register the economic activity and tax address, select applicable VAT and corporate tax census information, and identify the directors and beneficial owners as required.
required_dossiers: Economic activity classification and expected commencement date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct Form 036 errors, provide missing identification documents and respond through the AEAT electronic notification system.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authorized incorporation deed, name certificate, provisional NIF and registry forms electronically through the notary or directly where permitted. Pay the applicable regulated registry and official-gazette charges. Obtain the registration entry and definitive NIF update.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder documents, if incorporated into the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure a registry qualification by submitting a corrective deed, ratification, missing certificate or amended filing within the applicable defect-cure period. Appeal or seek judicial review of a final refusal under Spanish registry law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration tax, labor and municipal registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT; relevant municipality; General Treasury of Social Security (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social); regional labor authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Update the definitive NIF with AEAT, confirm census and VAT data, register as an employer before hiring personnel, enroll employees, assess municipal activity and works permits, and establish occupational-risk prevention arrangements before site operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to municipal or tax queries, amend activity codes and file corrected labor or census registrations before commencing the affected activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain industrial, energy-infrastructure and site operating approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent autonomous-community industry and energy authority; municipality; Ministry for Ecological Transition and Demographic Challenge or competent autonomous environmental authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the company is only a contractor or will own or operate terminal assets. For contracting, register and certify applicable industrial installations and qualified personnel. For ownership or operation, obtain project authorization, construction authorization, commissioning authorization and operating authorization for the gas infrastructure, together with environmental, hazardous-substance, pressure-equipment, fire and municipal approvals.
required_dossiers: Technical project signed by an authorized engineer
Gas infrastructure and pressure-equipment compliance files
Waste, emissions and discharge management procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to technical observations, revise the engineering project, obtain supplementary reports and request an administrative review or appeal against an adverse decision under the applicable energy, environmental and administrative-procedure rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The Industry and Energy Directorate of the autonomous community where the installation is located, applying Law 34/1998 on the Hydrocarbons Sector, Royal Decree 1434/2002, Royal Decree 919/2006 on gas installations, Royal Decree 809/2021 on pressure equipment and applicable autonomous-community industrial regulations. The Ministry for Ecological Transition and Demographic Challenge is competent for certain state-level gas infrastructure and environmental procedures.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Authorization for construction, commissioning and operation of the applicable gas infrastructure (autorización administrativa previa, autorización administrativa de construcción and autorización de explotación), together with registration or commissioning documentation for industrial, pressure, storage and cryogenic installations. A piping contractor must additionally hold the required habilitation or installer-company qualification for the regulated installation category.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition and Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), or the competent environmental authority of the autonomous community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-dependent. A standalone contracting activity is not automatically subject to EIA; an LNG receiving, storage or regasification terminal and associated major pipelines may require a full ordinary environmental impact assessment under Law 21/2013, its Annexes and applicable regional legislation. Smaller ancillary works may require simplified assessment, environmental screening or municipal environmental authorization.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges require authorization under the Water Law and Royal Legislative Decree 1/2001, with limits set by the basin authority or sewer operator and applicable treatment standards under Royal Decree 509/1996. VOC emissions are controlled under Royal Decree 117/2003 where listed solvent activities apply. Industrial emissions and best available techniques may apply under Royal Legislative Decree 1/2016 and Royal Decree 815/2013. Hazardous and non-hazardous waste must be segregated, stored, documented and transferred through authorized operators under Law 7/2022 and Royal Decree 553/2020. LNG, cryogenic releases, welding fumes and construction dust require site-specific monitoring and controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operation, obtain municipal building, works and activity approvals; fire-safety compliance under Royal Decree 2267/2004 for industrial establishments and Royal Decree 513/2017 for fire-protection installations; emergency planning and major-accident controls under Royal Decree 840/2015 where dangerous-substance thresholds are met; pressure-equipment inspection and conformity documentation under Royal Decree 809/2021; structural and load compliance under the Spanish Building Code and Royal Decree 470/2021 where applicable; and occupational-risk clearance under Law 31/1995, Royal Decree 39/1997 and relevant construction-safety rules. The operator must maintain emergency, evacuation, hot-work, confined-space, cryogenic-exposure and contractor-control procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT / 'Agencia Tributaria'); official portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Customs and Excise Department (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales) handles export procedures and the Export Declaration (DUA/EX).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Obtain a negative name certificate from the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central). 2) Open a Spanish corporate bank account and deposit share capital; no statutory minimum applies (EUR 3,000 default for an SL; EUR 1 is permissible under the 'Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva' regime). 3) Before notarization, apply to AEAT for a provisional NIF using Form 036 (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores), box 110. 4) Execute the incorporation deed before a Spanish notary and pay Capital Duty (ITP-AJD 'operaciones societarias', state rate 1%) within 30 days via Form 600. 5) Register the SL in the Provincial Mercantile Registry within 2 months of the deed. 6) Within 1 month of registry inscription, file Form 036 to obtain the definitive NIF; the SL receives a NIF of the format B + 8 digits + control character. 7) Complete the census filing (Form 036/037) including IAE activity enrollment, VAT position ('alta en IVA'), and enrollment in the 'Censo de Operadores Intracomunitarios' for EU cross-border supplies. The same NIF serves as the VAT ID; the intra-community VAT number is ES-BXXXXXXXX.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Spanish SL is a corporate vehicle tax-resident in Spain (place of incorporation and effective management), taxed on worldwide profits under the Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax, Law 27/2014). General corporate rate: 25%; newly incorporated active companies may benefit from a 15% reduced rate for the first two years of positive taxable base. No pass-through or check-the-box classification exists for an SL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not apply US-style check-the-box elections; legal-form classification is mandatory. Available statutory elections include: (a) joint tax consolidation for Spanish groups (at least 75% direct/indirect shareholding in Spanish or qualifying EU subsidiaries), IS arts. 67-78; (b) application of the reduced-size enterprise regime ('régimen de empresas de reducida dimensión') where turnover is below EUR 10 million; (c) VAT cash-basis regime ('régimen especial del criterio de caja') subject to the EUR 2 million turnover limit; (d) enrollment in the monthly VAT refund register allowing monthly filing and refunds, which also triggers SII real-time reporting obligations; (e) reverse-charge election for supplies to non-established B2B clients where the Spanish place-of-supply rules so permit; (f) application of anti-hybrid mismatch override rules in IS art. 15 to neutralize double non-taxation arising from hybrid instruments or entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_license_note: The ISIC 4322 activity (cryogenic stainless steel pipe welding and insulation contracting for LNG receiving terminals) requires a registered construction/installation company, qualified welding procedures per EN ISO 15614, and compliance with industrial safety licensing (e.g., R.D. 2267/2004 and applicable regional industrial regulations); the tax registration procedure described above runs in parallel with the sectoral license process.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (VAT), governed by Ley 37/1992, implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC. Territorial scope: Peninsular Spain and the Balearic Islands; the Canary Islands (IGIC), Ceuta and Melilla (IPSI, not VAT) are excluded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT exemption threshold for established business: every entrepreneur commencing economic activity must register in the census (Form 036) and obtain a NIF/VAT ID before supplying, with a zero-euro threshold. For intra-EU distance sales of goods to consumers, the OSS threshold is EUR 10,000 (EU-wide). Non-established foreign suppliers supplying B2B services to Spanish VAT-registered customers, or supplying construction services on Spanish real estate to a VAT-registered recipient, are normally relieved from Spanish VAT registration by the reverse-charge mechanism. For the local Spanish SL, mandatory registration applies in all cases regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Large taxpayers (turnover above EUR 6,010,121.04 or VAT-group members) are mandatorily enrolled in SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información): invoice-ledger records for issued and received invoices must be transmitted to AEAT through authenticated Web-Service APIs within 4 calendar days of the invoice event (with a maximum 8-day delay from the accrual of the supply). For all businesses, Verifactu (Real Decreto 1007/2023, effective for billing software produced after 1 July 2025) mandates certified billing software that generates an immutable, hash-linked 'Registro de Facturación' and a Verifactu QR code on invoices issued to final customers. The separate mandatory B2B electronic-invoicing duty under Law 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece') is adopted but not yet fully operative pending AEAT's implementation order; preparatory compliance with the 'Facturae' XML format (v3.2.x) and the FACE public reception platform is strongly recommended for construction-sector contracts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% ('exención plena' with right to deduct input VAT) is available for: (i) exports of goods physically leaving the EU customs territory, per art. 21 LIVA; (ii) transport and ancillary services directly linked to exported goods, per art. 22 LIVA; (iii) work performed on movable goods that remain outside the EU, per art. 23 LIVA; and (iv) intra-community supplies of goods to VAT-registered EU customers, per art. 25 LIVA, subject to VIES validation and the Form 349 recapitulative statement. The LNG terminal piping contracting activity, insofar as it constitutes installation or construction work on immovable property located inside Spain, falls under the Spanish place-of-supply rule (art. 70.Uno.2 LIVA) and is subject to 21% VAT, unless the domestic reverse-charge applies; zero-rating is only available where the welding/insulation work is performed on movable equipment destined for export or where the immovable works are physically located outside the EU, in which case the services fall outside the scope of Spanish VAT (subject to the non-established taxpayer refund regime for any residual Spanish input VAT).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Accepted Export Customs Declaration (DUA/EX) from the AEAT Customs system, including the ECS exit record and the proof of physical departure of the goods from the EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch
Bill of Lading (B/L), CMR with confirmed border exits, or Air Waybill evidencing the international carriage and the external destination

Commercial invoice bearing the clause 'Exento de IVA - Exportación / Art. 21 Ley 37/1992' (or 'Operación Intracomunitaria' with the EU customer's ES-prefixed VAT number and the applicable Intrastat/VIES data)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 evidencing collection of the foreign-currency payment on the exporter's Spanish bank account
Packing list, contract, weight or survey certificates, and, where the goods were moved under customs seal or temporary export, the customs control receipts confirming the closed itinerary
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT Inspection and the Customs Anti-Fraud units rigorously audit export zero-rating chains. The exporter must objectively and externally prove physical dispatch; if the DUA is revoked, the goods circulate domestically, the transport documents are simulated, or payment is not received without business justification, AEAT retroactively re-liquidates the 21% VAT (4-year limitation period), adds statutory late-payment interest (interés de demora), and imposes penalties under arts. 191-192 Ley General Tributaria 58/2003: 50% of the amount (no concealment), 100% (concealment), or up to 150% (use of false or fraudulent documents) plus loss of the monthly refund registration. Criminal tax evasion under art. 305 Código Penal applies where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period, exposing directors to imprisonment and the company to corporate penalties (art. 31 bis CP), administrative prohibition to contract with the public sector, and publication as a tax defaulter.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: European Central Bank (ECB) and Banco de España (BdE). The BdE is the Spanish national central bank and the competent authority for balance-of-payments statistical reporting, bank prudential supervision and foreign-exchange-related compliance under Law 12/1998 and Banco de España Circular 4/2012. The ECB governs euro monetary policy and TARGET2 settlement rails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a euro-area Member State with full current and capital account convertibility. The euro is freely convertible and there are no exchange controls or lump-sum conversion restrictions applicable to trade, investment, dividends, interest, royalties, profit remittances or liquidation proceeds. Capital movements are liberalised under Articles 63–65 TFEU and enforced through Spanish Law 12/1998. Practical hurdles are limited to: (i) balance-of-payments statistical declarations through banking entities; (ii) anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening; (iii) tax residence documentation for reduced withholding on remittances to non-resident shareholders; and (iv) the rare national-security foreign-investment screening applicable to critical infrastructure. None of these materially restrict a cryogenic LNG piping contractor from invoicing in EUR/USD or repatriating project profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no forced conversion ratio and no deadline for converting export proceeds. Exporters may lawfully retain foreign currency receipts abroad or in Spanish foreign-currency accounts. The only mandatory obligations are statistical and fiscal: banks report qualifying current transactions to the Banco de España on a monthly cycle for balance-of-payments purposes; exporters must maintain supporting documentation (contract, SWIFT MT103 credit advice, customs declarations if applicable, tax invoices). Foreign bank account or overseas equity balances exceeding relevant EUR thresholds must also be declared in the annual Modelo 720 information return. There is no surrender timeline; retention is unlimited.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BBVA, S.A. (Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A.)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a sole primary relationship bank; Medium as a complementary non-regulated payment rail. Spanish-regulated fintech EMIs such as Bnext or Rebellion, and EU-passported EMIs such as Revolut or Wise, can provide local Spanish IBANs and fast FX conversion, but they cannot issue documentary letters of credit, provide capital-deposit certificates required for an SL capital subscription, or substitute for a fully licensed credit institution under the Spanish AML and banking regime. A non-EU EMI is legally unsuitable for receiving shareholder capital contributions or high-value LNG terminal trade settlements. Use EMIs only for ancillary payroll, travel and small-project expenses.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is possible in principle under Spanish AML Law 10/2010, but in practice tier-1 banks require at least one physical interview at a Spanish branch for the legal representative when the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident. Fully remote opening may be granted only if video identification is performed through an accredited notary or certified e-ID provider and the signatory holds valid NIE and Cl@ve credentials. Most banks also require a notarial power of attorney and a certified corporate excerpt for non-resident directors. For the ES_SL, the prudent protocol is to have one director or a locally appointed financial controller attend the initial account-opening meeting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital subscription for the SL is made by a non-resident shareholder via foreign bank transfer without visible source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarially certified capital increase deed; bank certificate of deposit of capital; original SWIFT MT103; shareholder identity and NIE; three months' shareholder bank statements; audited parent-company financials; tax residence certificate; AML source-of-wealth declaration; registration excerpt from the Spanish Mercantile Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The LNG and cryogenic piping industry is classified as critical-infrastructure-adjacent, triggering sanctions and export-control sensitivity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate trade-compliance manual; end-user and end-use attestation; EU Dual-Use Regulation (EU) 2021/821 screening status; OFAC, EU and UN sanctions list verification of all project counterparties; contract with the Spanish LNG terminal operator; declaration that no sanctioned vessels, entities or nationals are involved in the welding, insulation or piping supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large advance payments from a foreign engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) prime or intercompany mobilisation payments in EUR/USD.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed works contract and statement of work; project milestone schedule; commercial invoice with ISIC 4322 project reference; SWIFT credit advices; independent engineer inspection certificates; third-party KYC questionnaire on the EPC counterparty; transfer pricing documentation for any intercompany margin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners or PEP status of minority shareholders triggers enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial-ownership register filing; FATF-compliant organisational chart; PEP declaration and respective source of wealth; valid passport or NIE for each shareholder; notarial power of attorney; CRS/FATCA self-certifications; corporate-service-provider declaration if nominee structures are present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to Latin American or offshore suppliers of cryogenic valves or welding inserts raise high-risk jurisdiction flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original purchase orders and zone-of-law explanations; letters of credit or bank payment evidence; shipping and customs documents; insurance certificates; supplier KYC pack and anti-bribery declaration; confirmation of tax withholding treatment; project-level transaction monitoring and escalation procedure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound protocol: (1) execute notarial capital-increase deed and deposit funds in an ES_SL capital account at a Spanish tier-1 bank; (2) transfer via SEPA Credit Transfer or SWIFT MT103/MT202, using purpose code CAPT (capital subscription) and referencing the Spanish NIF of the SL; (3) the bank will perform pre-credit KYC, sanctions screening and source-of-funds verification before crediting; (4) obtain the bank's capital-deposit certificate for the notary; (5) register the resulting foreign investment with the Spanish Register of Foreign Investments in the required filing window; (6) retain the SWIFT advice, shareholder resolution, notarial deed, bank statement and Mercantile Registry filing as the permanent proof-of-capital record. No prior Bank of Spain exchange authorisation is required, but the Bank of Spain statistical report must not be omitted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For procurement and subcontractor payments, use the following clearing rails: (i) SEPA B2B Credit Transfer for euro payments to EU suppliers; (ii) TARGET2/high-value euro payment for sums above the fast-transfer limit; (iii) SWIFT gpi MT103 / MT202 for USD or other non-euro trade payments, with full end-to-end reconciliation; (iv) documentary Letter of Credit issued under UCP600 for imported cryogenic materials and major plant components, preferably confirmed by a Spanish correspondent bank; and (v) conditional mobilisation payments via escrow or bank-guarantee-backed releases. All disbursements must reference the ES_SL tax identification and the ISIC 4322 project code; no cash, bearer instruments or third-party collect payments are permissible under the corporate treasury policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD forward contracts documented under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF deliverable foreign exchange forwards
FX swaps (spot versus forward or near-leg versus far-leg)
European-style currency options and zero-cost collars
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for medium-term LNG terminal project receivables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) exclusively for emerging-market currencies in Latin American supplier corridors where the local currency is not fully convertible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Directors' Report (Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Commercial Registry of the province where the SL has its registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by the Annual General Meeting within six months of the fiscal year-end (e.g., by 30 June for calendar-year entities); deposit with the Commercial Registry within one month of approval (e.g., by 30 July for calendar-year entities).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit incurs a fixed fine between €1,200 and €12,000 depending on turnover and capital; continued non-filing triggers closure of the company's registry sheet (cierre de la hoja registral), preventing registration of corporate acts and constituting administrative strike-off of the registry record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Spanish State Tax Administration Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year tax periods: from 1 July to 25 July of the following year. For non-calendar-year tax periods: within 25 calendar days after the six-month anniversary of the year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an additional surcharge (5% if filed within 6 months, 10% within 12 months, 15% after 12 months) plus late-payment interest; false or incomplete returns are subject to penalties of 50%–150% of the resulting quota and possible suspension of tax certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Titularidades Reales) operated through the Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fully integrated with the annual accounts deposit (Calendar-year deadline: by 30 July) and requiring confirmation of the UBO data on record; any change in beneficial ownership occurring during the year must be declared within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false statements carry administrative fines under Law 10/2010 on the prevention of money laundering; serious violations are penalised from €600 up to €60,000, with possible suspension of the company's entitlement to tax or public benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of statutory accounting books (Legalización de Libros de Contabilidad)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months from the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, on or before 30 April of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to legalise books prevents the approval and deposit of the next annual accounts; the books lose evidential value in commercial litigation and incur penalties of up to €1,200 under the Commercial Code.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SL must appoint a registered auditor (auditor de cuentas) when it meets, for two consecutive financial years, at least two of: (i) total assets exceeding €4,000,000; (ii) net turnover exceeding €8,000,000; (iii) an average number of employees exceeding 50. Listed, financial and other public-interest entities are always subject to statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts are prepared under Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, Royal Decree 1514/2007, as amended), aligned with EU Directive 2013/34/EU. Consolidated financial statements of groups are prepared under IFRS as endorsed by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 10/2010 and the UBO registry regulations, the SL must maintain a complete register of its ultimate beneficial owners. The annual accounts deposit includes a declaration confirming the UBOs; if no changes have occurred, the declaration operates as the annual confirmation. Any transfer of shareholding that modifies the UBO must be registered in the Commercial Registry and reported to the UBO registry within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500–$2,500 per year for professional registered-office or corporate-agent services (virtual office in Madrid/Barcelona)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,000–$15,000 per year for a ROAC-certified public audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for the first two years of profitable operations for newly created entities (subject to conditions). Tax credits for R&D, innovation, and export activities. Deductions for investments in renewable energy and intangible assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) via the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic filing system (Sede Electrónica).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 days following the 6-month period after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for calendar year-end, due by July 25 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number (NIF) of the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the NIF assigned by the Spanish tax authorities; non-resident entities must obtain a NIF via Form 036.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result (resultado contable) before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the net income per Spanish GAAP (PGC) as adjusted for permanent and temporary differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent differences (diferencias permanentes) – non-deductible expenses and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include non-deductible items such as fines, penalties, and 5% of the dividend received deduction (if applicable).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Temporary differences (diferencias temporarias) – timing differences (e.g., depreciation, provisions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for timing differences that reverse in future periods; maintain a reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base (base imponible) after offsetting prior-year tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the loss carryforward offset, subject to the annual limit (25% of taxable base for entities with net turnover ≥ €20M; 50% for smaller entities).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate applied (25% general, 15% for new entities in first two years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the applicable rate; non-resident entities without a permanent establishment are taxed at 25% on Spanish-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (deducciones) – R&D, export activities, etc.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits that are available to non-residents; verify treaty provisions and domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings and payments on account (retenciones y pagos a cuenta).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report any Spanish withholding taxes on income received (e.g., interest, royalties) and quarterly prepayments made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a refund is due, provide Spanish bank account details for transfer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. If no tax due, fixed penalty of €200. Surcharge for late payment: 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest (currently 3.75% per annum).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 222 (Pago fraccionado) – quarterly corporate income tax prepayment for entities with net turnover < €10 million; Form 202 for entities with net turnover ≥ €10 million. Filed via AEAT electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 20 days following the end of each quarter (April 20, July 20, October 20, and December 20 for the last quarter).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base for the quarter (based on the accounting result of the year-to-date).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a PE must file; those without a PE are not required to make quarterly prepayments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable percentage (for Form 222: 18% of the taxable base for entities with net turnover < €10 million; for Form 202: 25% for entities with turnover ≥ €10 million).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the correct percentage; non-residents with a PE follow the same rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction for prior quarterly payments made in the same fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Subtract cumulative payments to avoid overpayment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount to be paid (or refundable if negative).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Make payment via direct debit or bank transfer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due for the first month, plus 1% per additional month, up to 20%. Surcharge for late payment: 5% to 20% depending on delay, plus late interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (domestic withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must submit Form 210 (withholding tax return) and provide a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the residence country. The TRC must be apostilled or legalized (unless exempt under EU regulations). The payer must retain the TRC and apply the treaty rate at source. For EU/EEA shareholders, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) allows a 0% withholding if the parent holds at least 5% of the subsidiary's capital for at least 12 months. The process involves submitting Form 210 to claim a refund if the full 19% was withheld, or providing the TRC in advance to avoid over-withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for royalties and 25% for interest (unless exempt under EU Interest and Royalties Directive). Treaty rates: typically 5-10% for royalties and 5-10% for interest, depending on the DTA. For example, under the Spain-US DTA, royalty rate is 5% (for certain IP) and interest rate is 10%. Under the Spain-UK DTA, royalty rate is 5% and interest rate is 10%. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC) provides a 0% withholding for associated companies (25% ownership) within the EU.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 (net turnover) triggers mandatory Local File documentation. Master File is required if the group's consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000. Entities below the threshold must maintain simplified documentation (Form 232 summary).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime like the UAE, but the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) and the doctrine of 'substance over form' apply. For treaty benefits, the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) under the Multilateral Instrument (MLI) requires that the transaction has a genuine economic substance. A Spanish SL must demonstrate real business activity (e.g., employees, premises, operational functions) to avoid being classified as a shell company and to benefit from DTA relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating taxable income, inflating deductions, or failing to file tax returns to avoid tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty: 50% to 150% of the tax evaded (depending on the degree of concealment). Criminal liability: imprisonment from 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to 6 times the defrauded amount (if the amount exceeds EUR 120,000).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for the unpaid tax debt if they were involved in the evasion or failed to exercise due diligence. Civil restitution, travel bans, and disqualification from holding public office or managing companies for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Spanish SL without real economic activity, solely to obtain tax benefits or treaty relief, or to channel funds without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits (under PPT), recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of a 25% penalty on the tax avoided. The company may be liquidated and its corporate veil pierced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the company's tax debts if they knowingly used the entity as a shell. They may face criminal charges for tax fraud and be subject to travel bans and asset freezes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML controls (e.g., customer due diligence, record-keeping, reporting suspicious transactions) in a high-risk sector (cryogenic piping contracting with international payments via LC and SWIFT).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from EUR 60,000 to EUR 5,000,000 (depending on severity). Criminal liability for money laundering: imprisonment from 6 months to 6 years and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML breaches if they failed to appoint a compliance officer or implement controls. They may face criminal prosecution, travel bans, and disqualification from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain TP documentation, or applying non-arm's length prices in cross-border transactions with related parties (e.g., overpricing imports of materials or underpricing services).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalty of 15% on the adjusted amount (if documentation is incomplete) or 25% if no documentation is provided. Interest on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for the penalty if they signed the tax return and were aware of the non-compliance. They may face civil claims for damages and, in severe cases, criminal charges for tax evasion.
